prompt: Create a museum-quality cinematic identity master of Yinglong, the ancient Chinese winged rain dragon. Show one single complete creature in a three-quarter full-body view, with no rider and no other beings. Anatomy lock: one continuous elongated Chinese-dragon body from skull through long neck, deep ribcage, pelvis and one tapering tail; exactly four powerful legs with distinct shoulders, hips, joints and taloned feet; exactly one bilateral pair of enormous wings attached clearly to the upper back, each with a scaled leading edge, a restrained flexible inner membrane and layered indigo-black primary feathers; exactly two backward-sweeping branched ivory horns; exactly two eyes on one head. The head should read as an ancient Chinese dragon rather than a western fire dragon: long muzzle, strong brow, nostrils, whisker roots, cheek scales, modest dark mane, intelligent solemn expression. Materials: physically convincing overlapping bronze-green and deep teal scales with separated edges and directional relief, pale antique-gold segmented ventral scutes, indigo-black wing feathers with layered groups and subtle rain sheen, worn ivory keratin horns and claws, wet eyes and nostrils. Pose: grounded and dignified on a dark rain-wet stone ledge, torso seen clearly, wings lifted and opened enough to reveal their attachment and full silhouette, long tail sweeping behind without hiding any limb. Environment: the South Wilderness after a storm, distant floodplain and layered ink-dark mountains, low rain clouds parting around a restrained warm shaft of light; environment stays quieter and softer than the creature. Style: high-end cinematic creature design, realistic anatomy and PBR material study, ancient Chinese bronze and ink-painting sensibility without turning into a statue or painting. No text, labels, borders or watermark.
